rationale: This is a mechanical splice of two already-archived legs — the deleveraging × R&D-persistence interaction ("Liability-Light R&D Persistence") and the industry-relative organic-minus-goodwill mix ("Equity Cushion Organic Innovation Mix" / "Long-Maturity Organic Runway") — so it is a cosmetic recombination rather than a substantively new mechanism.

It is the archived "Uncollateralized R&D Rollover Load" with the denominator changed from ceq to at, a no-op WINSOR inside a RANK, and the expected sign reversed purely to match the earlier positive alpha, which is post-hoc sign-fitting rather than an economically motivated hypothesis.

The simplification from the archived rollover-acquisition tilt is genuinely motivated by the earlier alpha/t-stat divergence and the sign is coherent, though COALESCE(gdwl,0) plus ACCEL will leave a large mass of exact-zero ties that may make the industry rank leg mostly a goodwill-having dummy.

Because most firms have missing advertising coalesced to zero, the ad-intensity rank is heavily tied at the bottom and the signal collapses for most of the cross-section into liability growth × low sales growth, i.e. a repackaging of the well-known asset/liability-growth and sales-growth anomalies rather than the claimed brand-conversion channel; the level-versus-growth comparison also does not implement "not yet converting."

Swapping the sparse advertising leg for a better-covered R&D trend is a reasonable and internally consistent extension of the debt-retrenchment idea, but the net-debt-retirement leg is close to the standard net-debt-issuance anomaly, so the incremental content rests entirely on the modest R&D-trend interaction.

In Compustat, intan already includes gdwl, so DELTA(intan) and DELTA(gdwl) are mechanically near-collinear and the rank difference does not isolate identifiable intangibles as the hypothesis claims; additionally, multiplying by a positive-signed debt-issuance level contradicts the well-documented negative external-financing effect without any offsetting argument.
